checks.titleEn: GitHub Actions workflows have no security issues detected by zizmor
checks.condition: Scan GitHub Actions workflow files for security issues such as template injection, excessive permissions, unpinned actions, and other misconfigurations using the zizmor static analysis tool.
checks.remediation: Review your GitHub Actions workflows for security best practices including pinning actions to commit SHAs, using minimal permissions, avoiding template injection, and securing workflow triggers.

checks.titleEn: Organization prevents GitHub Actions from approving pull requests
checks.condition:
GitHub Actions organization settings define whether workflows are allowed to create and approve pull requests.

The evaluation determines whether that permission is disabled, so that approving a pull request always requires a human reviewer.
checks.remediation:
Disable Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests so that pull request approvals always come from a human reviewer.

Where automation genuinely needs to open pull requests, let it create them without granting approval rights, and keep the approval step with a reviewer who is not the author.

checks.titleEn: Organization base repository permission is read or none
checks.condition: GitHub organization base repository permission for members uses a strict setting such as read or none rather than permissive options like write or admin. *Applies to members, not outside collaborators.*
checks.remediation:
Apply least privilege: set base permission to none or read.

Grant higher access explicitly via teams per repo and enforce separation of duties with required reviews and branch protection. Regularly audit memberships and access to limit blast radius and maintain defense in depth.

checks.titleEn: Organization grants workflows a read-only default GITHUB_TOKEN
checks.condition:
GitHub Actions organization settings define the default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions granted to every workflow run.

The evaluation determines whether the organization default is read-only, so that workflows have to opt in to write access through an explicit permissions block.
checks.remediation:
Set the organization default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to read-only and grant write scopes per workflow with an explicit permissions block, following least privilege.

Also prevent Actions from approving pull requests, and prefer short-lived GitHub App tokens over broad credentials when a workflow genuinely needs write access.

checks.titleEn: Organization requires members to have two-factor authentication enabled
checks.condition:
GitHub organization settings require all members to use two-factor authentication (2FA).

The evaluation determines whether access to organization resources is conditioned on members having 2FA enabled.
checks.remediation:
Enforce org-wide 2FA for all members and collaborators, preferring secure methods (passkeys, security keys, authenticator apps, GitHub Mobile) over SMS.

Apply least privilege, integrate with SSO, restrict token scopes, and use branch protection for defense-in-depth. Include bots/service accounts and define recovery options.

checks.titleEn: Organization repository creation is limited to trusted members
checks.condition: GitHub organization repository creation is restricted so that only trusted owners or specific teams can create new repositories within the organization.
checks.remediation: Disable repository creation for members or limit it to specific trusted teams by adjusting Member privileges in the organization's settings.

checks.titleEn: Organization repository deletion and transfer is restricted to owners
checks.condition: Ensure repository deletion/transfer is restricted so only trusted organization users (owners) can delete or transfer repositories.
checks.remediation: Disable member repository deletion/transfer privileges so only organization owners can delete or transfer repositories.

checks.titleEn: Organization has a verified badge
checks.condition: GitHub organization has a verified badge.
checks.remediation: Verify the organization identity by completing GitHub organization verification.

checks.titleEn: Repository deletes branches after pull request merge
checks.condition: GitHub repository setting that enables automatic deletion of head branches when pull requests merge into the default branch (delete_branch_on_merge).
checks.remediation:
Enable automatic head-branch deletion after merges to minimize stale refs and confusion.
- Enforce least privilege for branch creation
- Apply branch protection and rulesets
- Prefer short-lived feature branches with periodic pruning
- Guard CI to avoid runs from obsolete branches

checks.titleEn: Repository denies default branch deletion
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch have branch protections or rulesets with Allow deletions disabled.
checks.remediation: Disable deletions on the default branch using branch protection or rulesets (Allow deletions=false). Apply controls to admins, minimize bypass lists, and enforce least privilege. Combine with required pull requests and status checks for defense in depth.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch denies force pushes
checks.condition:
GitHub repository default branch blocks force pushes through branch protection.

Evaluates whether the default branch permits force pushes. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation: Disable Allow force pushes on the default branch. Enforce PR-based changes with required reviews and status checks, require signed commits and linear history, and restrict bypass to minimal actors. Apply protections to admins too to uphold least privilege and defense in depth.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch dismisses stale pull request approvals
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch ensures that when new commits are pushed to an open pull request, any previously granted approvals are automatically dismissed, requiring fresh reviews before the pull request can be merged.
checks.remediation: Enable "Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed" in your branch protection rules. This ensures every code change undergoes a fresh review before merging.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch protection applies to administrators
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch applies branch protection rules to administrators via enforce_admins, holding admin pushes to the same requirements as other contributors (reviews, status checks, and push restrictions). This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation: Enable branch protection for administrators and disallow bypasses. Apply least privilege and separation of duties by requiring PR reviews, required status checks, and signed commits on critical branches. Limit force pushes and deletions, and regularly review admin roles and audit logs.

checks.titleEn: Repository enforces branch protection on the default branch
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch has branch protection rules enabled to restrict direct changes and require reviewed, validated merges. The evaluation determines whether the default branch enforces such rules. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enforce branch protection on the default branch:
- Require pull requests with approvals (least privilege)
- Enforce required status checks and conversation resolution
- Require signed commits and linear history; block force pushes/deletions
- Restrict push to trusted actors and apply rules to admins
Use CODEOWNERS to strengthen review accountability.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires code owner approval for changes to owned code
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch requires Code Owners approval for pull requests that modify paths declared in CODEOWNERS. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enforce Code Owners review on the default branch and keep CODEOWNERS accurate and team-based.
Apply least privilege, require status checks and signed commits, extend protections to admins, and audit ownership regularly. Co-own critical paths to ensure coverage and reduce single-point approval gaps.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires conversation resolution before merging
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch uses branch protection to require conversation resolution on pull requests (Require conversation resolution before merging). This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enable Require conversation resolution before merging on the default branch.

Also enforce:
- Required approvals and CI checks
- CODEOWNERS on critical paths
- Least privilege for merge rights
- Apply rules to admins to prevent bypass

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires linear history
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch enforces Require linear history, blocking merge commits and allowing only squash or rebase merges. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enable Require linear history on the default branch and allow only squash or rebase merges.

Reinforce with branch protection: require pull requests and reviews, status checks, and signed commits. Limit bypass to trusted roles (least privilege) to preserve traceability and defense in depth.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires at least 2 approvals for code changes
checks.condition:
GitHub repository default branch enforces required reviews with a minimum of 2 approving reviews before a pull request can be merged.

Assesses whether an approval threshold of at least 2 is configured for code changes targeting the default branch. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enforce the four-eyes principle by requiring at least 2 approvals for merges to the default branch.

Strengthen with separation of duties using code owner reviews, dismiss stale approvals, apply protections to admins, and pair with required status checks for defense in depth.

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires signed commits
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch enforces signed and verified commits (Require signed commits), allowing only commits with valid cryptographic signatures to be pushed or merged. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enforce Require signed commits on default and release branches.
- Standardize GPG/SSH/S/MIME for humans and bots
- Protect and rotate signing keys; least privilege on bypass
- Pair with required reviews and status checks for defense-in-depth

checks.titleEn: Repository default branch requires status checks
checks.condition: GitHub repository default branch uses required status checks, indicating whether merges are gated by successful check results on pull requests. This protection can be enforced through classic branch protection or repository rulesets.
checks.remediation:
Enforce branch protection to require status checks on the default branch.
- Gate merges on build, tests, and security scans
- Use require up-to-date behavior to reduce integration risk
- Apply to admins and limit bypasses
- Combine with least privilege and required reviews for defense in depth

checks.titleEn: Repository grants workflows a read-only default GITHUB_TOKEN
checks.condition:
GitHub Actions repository settings define the default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions granted to every workflow run in the repository.

The evaluation determines whether the repository default is read-only, so that workflows have to opt in to write access through an explicit permissions block.
checks.remediation:
Set the repository default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to read-only and grant write scopes per workflow with an explicit permissions block, following least privilege.

A repository can override an organization default, so verify this setting per repository even when the organization already defaults to read-only. Prefer short-lived GitHub App tokens over broad credentials when a workflow genuinely needs write access.

checks.titleEn: Repository has package vulnerability scanning (Dependabot alerts) enabled
checks.condition: GitHub repositories are assessed for dependency vulnerability scanning enabled via Dependabot alerts, which monitors the dependency graph for known vulnerable packages and versions.
checks.remediation: Enable dependency vulnerability scanning with Dependabot alerts or an equivalent SCA tool across repositories. Apply defense in depth: keep manifests and lockfiles current, triage alerts quickly, use automated security updates with required reviews, and surface results in PR checks and notifications.

checks.titleEn: Repository has a CODEOWNERS file
checks.condition: GitHub repositories declare code ownership via a CODEOWNERS file mapping file patterns to users or teams. This evaluation checks whether such a file exists in standard locations (/, .github/, or docs/) to enable automatic reviewer assignment.
checks.remediation: Define and maintain a CODEOWNERS file mapping sensitive paths to responsible teams or users, preferring teams for resilience. Combine with branch protections requiring code-owner reviews to enforce separation of duties and least privilege. Keep entries current and cover critical directories to avoid pattern gaps.

checks.titleEn: Repository has immutable releases enabled
checks.condition: GitHub repository has immutable releases enabled to prevent modification or replacement of published artifacts after publication. When enabled, release assets and binaries become tamper-proof, ensuring artifact integrity throughout the software supply chain.
checks.remediation: Enable immutable releases in the repository settings so release artifacts cannot be altered once published.

checks.titleEn: Repository is archived or active within the configured inactivity threshold
checks.condition: GitHub repository that remains unarchived and show no activity beyond a configured inactivity window (e.g., 180 days) are identified. The evaluation considers the most recent repository activity to surface long-idle codebases that are still unarchived.
checks.remediation:
Adopt lifecycle management:
- Archive or delete repos no longer needed
- If retained, update dependencies, rotate secrets, disable unused workflows, and restrict writes under least privilege
- Define an inactivity policy (e.g., 180 days) with periodic reviews to prevent dormant, writable codebases

checks.titleEn: Public repository has a SECURITY.md file
checks.condition: GitHub public repository include a SECURITY.md policy file that tells researchers how to report vulnerabilities. The evaluation focuses on the presence of this file in public repositories.
checks.remediation: Publish a clear SECURITY.md for each public repo or an org default. Include private reporting channels, optional encryption keys, scope/supported versions, disclosure timelines, and safe-harbor terms. Link to any bounty program and review regularly. Align with accountability and defense in depth principles.

checks.titleEn: Repository has secret scanning enabled to detect sensitive data
checks.condition: GitHub repository configuration for secret scanning-which detects secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) in commits and Git history-is evaluated to determine if detection is active.
checks.remediation:
Enable secret scanning (and push protection where available) across repositories.
- Store secrets in a dedicated secrets manager, never in code
- Define custom patterns and enable generic detection for org-specific secrets
- Rotate and revoke exposed credentials quickly
- Enforce least privilege and add defense-in-depth monitoring
